extracted.intended_audience: writers and readers of heroic/religious biography; students of literature and creative-writing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for depicting and evaluating heroic/religious figures in prose: what makes a hero, what makes a religious text or life convincing, and the literary qualities that matter (sincerity, vision, authenticity vs. mere polish).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hero's primary distinction: 'looks through the shows of things into things'
rubrics_metrics.description: A Hero, ... has this first distinction, which indeed we may call first and last, the Alpha and Omega of his whole Heroism, That he looks through the shows of things into things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not content with use, wont, respectable hearsay or formula; the heroic character is defined by the capacity to see the underlying Reality (not mere appearances or 'idolatries'). The hero must answer essential existential questions for himself rather than accept received formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity as the first and last merit in a book
rubrics_metrics.description: Sincerity, in all senses, seems to me the merit of the Koran; ... It is, after all, the first and last merit in a book; gives rise to merits of all kinds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book that truly comes from the heart will reach other hearts despite faults of style or form; sincerity is the foundational quality from which other literary merits arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuineness of heart (bona-fide authenticity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary character of the Koran is this of its genuineness, of its being a bona-fide book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature judges a thing by its genuine heart: 'She requires of a thing only that it be genuine of heart; she will protect it if so.' The decisive question is not purity from all chaff but whether there is any wheat—i.e., an authentic core.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-operating with the real Tendency of the World (resigned submission) as moral criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A man is right and invincible, virtuous and on the road towards sure conquest, precisely while he joins himself to the great deep Law of the World... This is the soul of Islam; it is properly the soul of Christianity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral worth is judged by alignment with the world's deep order or law (a resigned submission to what is morally real), rather than by superficial social success or ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive intensity can outweigh compositional polish
rubrics_metrics.description: The Koran ... is a wearisome confused jumble, crude, incondite; endless iterations ... yet when once you get this confused coil fairly off your hands ... the essential type of it begins to disclose itself; and in this there is a merit quite other than the literary one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A text's breathless intensity, urgency, or oral/rhythmic power (especially true of extempore or orally rooted works) can deliver meaning and move readers even if the composition lacks method, order, or classical polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess living effect over logical correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Not that Abstractions, logical Propositions, be correctly worded or incorrectly; but that living concrete Sons of Adam do lay this to heart: that is the important point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious or philosophical writings should be evaluated by their capacity to move, change, or live in people's hearts and lives, not merely by doctrinal precision or logical formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess prophetic legitimacy by life-character and sincerity, not by charge of imposture
rubrics_metrics.description: We will leave it altogether, this impostor hypothesis, as not credible ... he lived in this entirely unexceptionable, entirely quiet and commonplace way, till the heat of his years was done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging a claimed prophet or charismatic figure, consider their prior life, consistency, and evidence of sincere conviction (steady domestic conduct, years of ordinary behaviour) rather than assuming deliberate fraud because their later mission brought ambition or success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature as umpire: truth endures despite admixture of error
rubrics_metrics.description: On the whole, a thing will propagate itself as it can. ... Nature herself is umpire, and can do no wrong: the thing which is deepest-rooted in Nature, what we call truest, that thing and not the other will be found growing at last.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ideas and movements by their long-term vitality and capacity to produce what is genuinely life-giving; temporary success or roughness does not disqualify a genuine truth-seed that will ultimately flourish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary merit includes capacity for direct insight ('sincerity of vision')
rubrics_metrics.description: The eye that flashes direct into the heart of things, and sees the truth of them; this is to me a highly interesting object... it is what I call sincerity of vision; the test of a sincere heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond formal qualities, value writing that contains direct, original insight into human or natural reality—a clear, affecting vision—even if it appears rugged or unpolished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral/rhythmic form and communal use can compensate for textual disorder
rubrics_metrics.description: Mahomet's followers found the Koran lying all in fractions ... and they published it, without any discoverable order ... Much of it, too, they say, is rhythmic; a kind of wild chanting song, in the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a work originates in oral performance or communal practice, its authority and power may reside in rhythm, repetition, and use rather than in linear textual order; evaluation should account for performative qualities and reception.
